belief: It runs in my family, so I'm doomed.
origins: Watching a parent or relative suffer from a disease, addiction, or mental illness can make us feel that the same fate is sealed. Family patterns are real risk factors, but risk is not destiny, and fear of fate can paralyze us.
teaches: God told Israel, “A son will not bear the iniquity of his father” (Ezekiel 18:20), and “each is to die for his own sin” (Deuteronomy 24:16). Moses wrote that the LORD is “compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion.” Jeremiah heard, “I know the plans I have for you… plans to prosper you and not to harm you, to give you a future and a hope.” Genes may raise a risk, but choices, treatment, support, and God’s grace matter. Many who are at risk never develop the condition, and many who do live well with it.
self_statements: My family curse will find me.
errors: Believing I either have no risk or am doomed.
Predicting that I will repeat the family pattern.
Feeling afraid and concluding that it is inevitable.
questions: What does my doctor say about my actual risk?
What steps can lower the risk or catch it early?
What did my relative lack that I can have, such as treatment, support, or knowledge?
Do I know family members who faced the same risk and did well?
What does Scripture say about inherited guilt?
What is one preventive step I can take?
truth: Risk is not destiny. God has plans for my future and hope, and I can take wise steps, get good medical advice, and trust Him with what I cannot control.
hw_truths: A son will not bear his father’s iniquity.
God has plans for my future and hope.
He will fulfill His purpose for me.
log: Each month, note one healthy or preventive step you took.
actions: Ask your doctor about screening and prevention.
Sleep, move, eat well, and reduce harmful substances.
Talk to a counselor if fear dominates.
prayer: Lord, I fear what runs in my family. Give me wisdom, wise doctors, and trust that my future is in Your hands. Amen.
